title: Density Gradient Fractionation of RNA from RNA-SIP Experiments
author: Julie Huber
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.iu2ceye
materials: Prime tubing with colored MilliQ water.
Screw needle on end of tubing, prime again.
Puncture the bottom of 5ml tube with needle.

steps.title: Prepare consumables and reagents
steps.instruction: Make 70 % ethanol and store in freezer; aliquot 100 % isopropanol into a 50 ml tube and store in freezer; prepare ~50 ml colored MilliQ water with food dye or 500 µl Resazurin; autoclave tubing for low‑flow pump; set up a ring stand with a test‑tube clamp; sterilize and label 1.5 ml tubes for each sample (labels 1‑12, 24 tubes per rack for two samples).

steps.title: Label tubes and plan samples
steps.instruction: Label 15 ml tubes with sample names, using no more than 6‑8 samples per run and always including at least one No‑RNA control.

steps.title: Add CsTFA to tubes
steps.instruction: Using a 5 ml syringe with a 0.2 µm filter, add 5 ml of CsTFA to each tube, then add an additional 0.1 ml with a 1 ml syringe and 0.2 µm filter (total 5.1 ml CsTFA per tube).

steps.title: Add formamide
steps.instruction: Add 185 µl formamide to each tube; store formamide in small aliquots at –20 °C to minimise degradation.

steps.title: Add Gradient Salt Solution and RNA
steps.instruction: Add Gradient Salt Solution to bring the volume to 1 ml after accounting for the RNA volume (e.g., for 20 µl RNA add 980 µl Gradient Salt Solution). Then add 750 ng RNA (acceptable range 500‑750 ng).

steps.title: Mix gently
steps.instruction: Mix the tube gently by inverting; do NOT vortex.

steps.title: Calibrate refractometer
steps.instruction: Set the refractometer to the nd‑TC setting and calibrate using MilliQ water.

steps.title: Measure and adjust RI
steps.instruction: Pipette 75 µl from each tube and measure the refractive index (RI). Acceptable RI is 1.3729 ± 0.0002. If RI is low, add 50‑100 µl CsTFA; if high, add 50‑100 µl Gradient Salt Solution. Mix and re‑measure until within range. Also measure pure CsTFA each time to monitor density changes.

steps.title: Fill Beckman tubes and record mass
steps.instruction: Rinse 5 ml Beckman ultracentrifuge tubes with 70 % ethanol and dry. Using a 5 ml serological pipette, fill each tube to the bottom of the neck (do not overfill) and place a black cap on top. Determine the mass of each filled tube on a scale (place tube in a small beaker for easier weighing) and ensure masses are comparable.

steps.title: Balance tubes in rotor
steps.instruction: Pair tubes with similar masses, load them into the rotor, and balance the rotor. Place gold caps on top of the tubes, thread the caps, and tighten with a ratchet.

steps.title: Ultracentrifuge gradient
steps.instruction: Insert the rotor into the ultracentrifuge and run at 37 000 rpm, 20 °C for more than 60 hours (commonly 64 hours). Ensure the program is set with NO BRAKE for deceleration.

steps.title: Unload rotor and rack tubes
steps.instruction: Remove the rotor from the ultracentrifuge, unload the tubes, and place them in a black rack.

steps.title: Set up fraction collector pump
steps.instruction: Set the low‑flow pump to 0.42 ml/min. Clamp the 5 ml tube (containing the gradient) on a ring stand and arrange the labeled 1.5 ml collection tubes beneath it, ensuring tube 1 (the heaviest fraction) is positioned first and its cap is open.

steps.title: Collect fractions
steps.instruction: Puncture the top of the 5 ml tube with a primed needle attached to the tubing. Start a 12‑minute timer and simultaneously start the pump. Every minute, shift the rack so that the next 1.5 ml tube receives the flow, collecting approximately 420 µl per tube.

steps.title: Measure RI of fractions
steps.instruction: Measure and record the RI of each fraction. Fractions 6‑7 (the middle fractions) should have an RI of ~1.3729. If they differ, the fractionation may need to be repeated.

steps.title: Repeat fractionation for samples
steps.instruction: Perform the entire fractionation procedure for each sample.

steps.title: Precipitate RNA with isopropanol
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of ice‑cold 100 % isopropanol to each fraction tube, mix gently by inverting, and incubate in the freezer for more than 30 minutes (overnight incubation is acceptable).

steps.title: Centrifuge and wash RNA pellet
steps.instruction: Spin the tubes for 25 minutes in a microcentrifuge located in a cold room to pellet the RNA. Carefully pipet off the supernatant without disturbing the pellet, then add 150 µl of 70 % ethanol to wash the pellet.
